title: Profit targets, your monthly P&L and cash flow

say: Profit targets, your monthly profit and loss, and cash flow.
This is the video for Module 3 of Pricing, Costing and Profit Planning.
Break-even tells you how to stop losing money. A profit target tells you how to make the money you want. Just add the profit you want to your fixed costs, then divide by your contribution per unit.

card.title: Work back from the profit you want

say: Ngozi's fixed costs are 110,000 naira a month. Her own wage is already inside them.

card.title: Work back from the profit you want

say: She wants 100,000 naira profit on top, to save for a bigger fryer.

card.title: Work back from the profit you want
rows: Target profit for a bigger fryer

say: Together that is 210,000 naira. Divided by 760, that is 276.3. Round up: 277 packs a month.
That becomes 70 packs a week, or 11 packs a day. A number she can tick off in her notebook.

card.title: Work back from the profit you want
rows: Target profit for a bigger fryer

say: A target is only useful if you can reach it. Can you make it? Ngozi can fry 6 to 8 batches a month, so yes.

say: Can you sell it? She sold about 250 packs last month, so 277 is a stretch of about 11 percent, not a fantasy.

say: Then choose your lever: raise the price, cut variable cost, cut fixed cost, or sell more. At 1,500 naira, Ngozi would need 375 packs for the same profit. Low prices demand far more work and cash.

say: A profit and loss statement is your monthly scorecard. Start with sales: everything you sold, including sales on credit.
Subtract the cost of goods sold. That is the variable cost of the units you actually sold.
That gives gross profit. Units still on your shelf are stock, not this month's cost.

panel.heading: Your monthly profit and loss
panel.rule: Count only the variable cost of units sold. Unsold units are stock.

say: Subtract your operating expenses: rent, your wage, data, levies and equipment wear.

panel.heading: Your monthly profit and loss
panel.rule: Count only the variable cost of units sold. Unsold units are stock.

say: What is left is your net profit, or net loss. With good daily records, this takes about 30 minutes.

panel.heading: Your monthly profit and loss
panel.rule: Count only the variable cost of units sold. Unsold units are stock.

say: Here is a real month. Ngozi made 350 packs. She sold 260 at 1,700 naira and 60 at 1,400 naira, and 30 were still in stock.
Her total sales were 526,000 naira.
320 packs sold, at 940 naira each, is 300,800 naira cost of goods sold. Her gross profit is 225,200 naira.
After 110,000 naira of operating expenses, her net profit is 115,200 naira. That beats her target by 15,200 naira.
Watch your gross margin and net margin each month. Hers are about 42.8 percent and 21.9 percent.
Cash flow is the actual movement of money in and out. Many small businesses fail not because they are unprofitable, but because they run out of cash.
Credit sales count as sales, but no cash arrives until the customer pays.

cards.d: Counted as sales in the P&L, but no cash arrives until the customer pays.
You paid cash to make it, but it is not yet a cost in the P&L.
Cash leaves, but repaying the loan amount is not an expense in the P&L.

say: Ngozi made 115,200 naira profit. So where is her cash?
Only her retail sales, 442,000 naira, came in. The supermarket's 84,000 naira is not due until next month.
Out went 466,000 naira for 7 batches, fixed costs and the loan repayment.
Her cash fell to 16,000 naira, not enough for even one 47,000 naira batch. That is why you forecast cash week by week, and act early on any week that ends negative.
Take a deposit, for example 50 percent, before starting custom orders. Give credit only to known customers, in writing, with a due date. Keep a buffer of at least one month of fixed costs.
Do not borrow to cover a loss. And be wary of investment offers promising high monthly returns.

panel.heading: Protect your cash
items: Take a deposit on custom orders
Write credit amounts and due dates
Keep one month of fixed costs as a buffer
Never borrow to hide a loss

say: To remember. Add your profit target to fixed costs and divide by contribution. Turn it into a daily number. Build your P&L every month. Remember that profit is not cash. And forecast cash weekly, so you act before a week goes negative.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Turn the target into daily numbers
Sales, minus COGS, minus expenses = net profit
Profit is not cash: credit, stock and loans
Forecast cash weekly; act on negative weeks

say: Now set your own profit target with daily and weekly numbers, prepare last month's profit and loss, and build a four-week cash forecast.
